memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"Then they came to Elim, where there were twelve springs and seventy palm trees,
and they camped there near the water." - Ex 15:27 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
And then, Elim. Twelve springs and seventy palm trees.

There is such kindness in this verse. After three days of thirst and a bitter
disappointment, God brings them to abundance. Not one spring, but twelve. Not a
patch of shade, but seventy palms. And the text simply says they camped there
near the water.

Notice that Elim was always there. It existed while they were thirsty at Marah.
God knew the whole time that Elim was two days ahead.

That is worth holding when you are in a dry stretch. The provision may already
exist and simply be further along the road than you can see.

Notice too what they did at Elim: they camped. They stopped and rested. God gives
seasons of refreshment, and it is not unspiritual to enjoy them. Some believers
feel guilty resting, as though only the hard seasons are serious. Jesus told His
disciples, "Come with me by yourselves to a quiet place and get some rest"
(Mark 6:31).

Elim was not the promised land. They would move on, and there would be more
wilderness. But God gave them a place to breathe on the way.

If you are at Elim today, drink deeply and rest well.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Are you at Marah or at Elim right now?
2. Do you allow yourself to rest and enjoy God's provision without guilt?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Father, thank You for the places of rest You provide along the way. Help me to
receive them gratefully and not feel guilty for resting. Amen.
